newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BRUSSELS BOURSE SEEN CONSOLIDATING IN DAYS AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS BOURSE SEEN CONSOLIDATING IN DAYS AHEAD.

text.p: Belgian shares, which closed marginally lower on Wednesday, are seen consolidating in the days ahead as the market digests recent sharp gains.
The Bel-20 index ended 6.86 points or 0.10 percent lower at 2,109.49 after spending the day in a tight 20-point range.
Dealers said the Dow Jones and the dollar would keep on setting the trend in Brussels.
Luxembourg steel maker Arbed SA was the star performer. The share, catching up with other recent gainers in the steel sector, ended 4.7 percent higher at 3,770 francs.
Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) closed 0.7 percent higher at 2,805 francs in busy trade of 64,343 shares.

SGB, a unit of French Compagnie de Suez , declined to comment on news that French fund managers are saying that SGB is selling an eight percent stake in French hotel group Accor at 756 francs per share.
Analysts have repeatedly said that it would make sense for SGB to sell Accor, as the stake does not fit with the group's tradition of holding controlling stakes.
